baseline.authority: docs/design/PO_DECISION_RECORD_2026_09_15C_REGRESSION_GATE_RUNS_WHEN_THE_CORE_CHANGES.md section 7 (FROZEN, 2026-09-16). baseline.observed: NXS-LOCAL-0350 was dispatched with an instruction to route unmapped and persistence-only changes to the full regression. That contradicted the frozen record, the engineer raised it as a RELAY_QUESTION rather than reconciling two authorities, and the Product Owner answered at seq 3 of that movement's record: the frozen record governs, the mapping is extended instead of the fallback, and visible blocking stays. This movement carries the corrected instruction. The defect that remains real and is not resolved by the frozen record: scripts/ci_regression_scope.py maps ui2/persistence/ and ui2/service/ wholesale to the approved LDAP delivery's fixed targeted selection, so a change to either that has nothing to do with that delivery reaches a green gate having run none of the tests that cover it. Pull request 434 would have done exactly that had it not also touched frontend files, because JooqDeviceRepositoryTest and TopologyNamePseudonymizerTest match none of the LDAP filters.

recommended_reasoning.reason: A bounded change to one classifier, one workflow job and their tests. The authority conflict is already resolved and recorded, and the separation constraint is stated here, so no design question is left open.

requirements: Discovery and inventory are separate mapped components. They are never folded into one entry, never share a selection, and neither is reachable through the other's paths. The Product Owner's reason, recorded so it is not lost: they are two features and are intended to become two separate microservices.
Each mapped component names the tests that cover it, so that a green gate means those tests ran
A change spanning several mapped components runs the union of their selections
A change inside the approved LDAP delivery keeps its existing selection unchanged
A change to ui2/persistence or ui2/service that lies outside the LDAP delivery no longer inherits that delivery's selection
An unmapped path, an empty path set, or a failed selector still blocks visibly
A documentation-only change still routes to skip, and the major prefixes still route to full
risks: Narrowing ui2/persistence and ui2/service will block changes that previously passed. That is the correction, not a regression: they were passing on tests that did not cover them. Do not offset it by widening a selection.

The workflow currently has one targeted job with a hardcoded command list. Supporting several components may need either one job per component or a selection the job reads from the classifier. Choose the smaller change that keeps the mapping auditable, and state which you chose and why in the SESSION_CLOSE.
scripts/ci_regression_scope.py is itself in the delivery file set, so this movement's own pull request routes through the mapping it changes. Verify its own gate behaves as expected.
